meta.stack: Laravel 13 (PHP 8.3+) · MySQL 8 · Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite + Pinia
meta.roles: Admin, Agent (requesters are contact records, not logins)
meta.note: Single source of truth for the Jira backlog. Edit here, re-run upload.mjs.

epics.goal: Stand up the monorepo, the Laravel 13 API, the Vue 3 SPA and a one-command local environment so every later epic has somewhere to land.

stories.want: a monorepo with backend/, frontend/, docs/ and tools/ plus a root README and .gitignore
stories.soThat: the whole team works from one predictable layout
acceptanceCriteria: Repository initialised with git and a root .gitignore covering vendor/, node_modules/, .env, .jira.env and build output
Root README documents the layout, prerequisites and how to start the stack
docs/ contains a placeholder for the ERD, API contract and deployment runbook
tools/jira/.jira.env is git-ignored and never committed

stories.summary: Install and configure the Laravel 13 API
stories.want: Laravel 13 installed in backend/ with MySQL 8 configured and a health endpoint
stories.soThat: I can prove the PHP and database layers talk to each other before building features
acceptanceCriteria: Laravel 13 installed via composer, running on PHP 8.3+
backend/.env.example documents every variable the app needs, with no real secrets
Database connection points at MySQL 8 and php artisan migrate runs clean
GET /api/v1/health returns 200 with app version and database connectivity status
API routes are versioned under /api/v1 from the very first route

stories.summary: Scaffold the Vue 3 SPA with an API client
stories.want: a Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite SPA with Vue Router, Pinia and a configured axios client
stories.soThat: the frontend can call the API with auth headers from day one
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/ scaffolded with Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, Vue Router and Pinia
src/api/client.ts exposes an axios instance reading the base URL from an env variable
A request interceptor attaches the bearer token and a response interceptor redirects to login on 401
The SPA successfully calls /api/v1/health and renders the result
Vite dev server proxies API calls so there are no CORS issues in development

stories.summary: One-command local environment with Docker Compose
stories.want: docker-compose.yml providing MySQL 8 and Mailpit
stories.soThat: any machine can run the stack without installing database or mail servers locally
acceptanceCriteria: docker compose up -d starts MySQL 8 and Mailpit with healthchecks
MySQL data persists in a named volume across restarts
Mailpit UI is reachable and Laravel mail config points at it in development
Ports and credentials come from environment variables with documented defaults
README documents the full start, stop and reset sequence

stories.summary: Code quality tooling and CI pipeline
stories.want: Pint, ESLint, Prettier and a CI workflow that runs linters and tests on every push
stories.soThat: style drift and broken code are caught before review, not during it
acceptanceCriteria: php artisan pint --test passes on the backend
npm run lint and npm run format:check pass on the frontend
GitHub Actions workflow runs backend tests, frontend tests and both linters
CI spins up a MySQL 8 service so backend feature tests run against a real database
The workflow fails the build on any linter or test failure

epics.goal: Token-based authentication with two roles (admin, agent), admin-managed agent accounts, and authorization enforced by policies on both the API and the SPA.

stories.summary: Users table with role enum and a seeded admin
stories.want: the users migration with a role enum plus a seeder creating the first admin
stories.soThat: a fresh install can be logged into immediately
acceptanceCriteria: users table has name, email (unique), password, role enum('admin','agent'), is_active and timestamps
A PHP 8.3 backed enum UserRole is the single definition of the role values
Seeder creates one admin whose credentials come from environment variables, not hardcoded
The seeder is idempotent and safe to run twice

stories.summary: Log in and receive an API token
stories.want: to log in with my email and password and receive a Sanctum token
stories.soThat: I can access the protected parts of the system
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/auth/login validates credentials and returns a token plus the user object
Invalid credentials return 422 with a generic message that does not reveal whether the email exists
A deactivated user (is_active = false) cannot log in even with a correct password
The login route is rate limited to a small number of attempts per minute per IP
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never appear in any API response

stories.summary: Log out and revoke the token
stories.want: to log out and have my token deleted server side
stories.soThat: a stolen token cannot be reused after I leave
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/auth/logout deletes the current access token and returns 204
Reusing the revoked token afterwards returns 401
GET /api/v1/auth/me returns the authenticated user for a valid token

stories.summary: SPA session persistence and route guards
stories.want: the SPA to remember my session, guard private routes and bounce me to login when my token expires
stories.soThat: I am never stranded on a broken screen
acceptanceCriteria: A Pinia auth store holds the token and user and rehydrates on page reload
Router guard redirects unauthenticated users to /login and preserves the intended destination
Admin-only routes are blocked for agents with a clear not-authorised screen
A 401 from any request clears the store and redirects to login exactly once, without a redirect loop
Logging out clears the persisted token from storage

stories.want: to create, edit and deactivate agent accounts from a Users screen
stories.soThat: I control exactly who can access the system
acceptanceCriteria: Users list shows name, email, role, active state and ticket count, paginated and searchable
Admin can create a user, choosing the admin or agent role, with validation on a unique email
Admin can edit a user's name, email and role, and toggle is_active
Deactivating rather than deleting is the default, so ticket history keeps a valid author
An admin cannot deactivate or demote their own account, preventing lockout

stories.want: authorization enforced by Laravel policies on every endpoint
stories.soThat: an agent cannot reach admin functionality by calling the API directly
acceptanceCriteria: UserPolicy, CategoryPolicy and TicketPolicy define who may view, create, update and delete
Every controller action authorizes before acting; no endpoint relies on the UI hiding a button
An agent calling an admin-only endpoint receives 403, verified by a feature test per endpoint
Policy logic reads the UserRole enum rather than comparing raw strings

stories.want: to change my password by confirming the current one
stories.soThat: I can rotate my credentials without asking an admin
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/v1/auth/password requires the current password and a confirmed new password
New password is validated against a minimum strength rule
All other tokens for that user are revoked after a successful change
A wrong current password returns 422 without changing anything

epics.goal: Admin-managed master data that classifies every ticket, with statuses held in a table rather than an enum so the workflow stays configurable.

stories.want: categories, priorities and statuses tables seeded with sensible defaults
stories.soThat: tickets can be classified the moment the app is installed
acceptanceCriteria: categories table has name, slug, description, color, is_active, sort_order, timestamps and soft deletes
priorities table has name, slug, level, color and is_default, seeded with Low, Medium, High and Urgent
statuses table has name, slug, bucket, color, is_default, is_terminal and sort_order, seeded with New, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed and Reopened
Exactly one priority and one status are marked is_default
Seeders are idempotent and keyed on slug so re-running does not duplicate rows

stories.want: to create, edit, reorder and deactivate ticket categories
stories.soThat: classification matches how our support team actually works
acceptanceCriteria: Full CRUD available at /api/v1/categories, restricted to admins for writes and open to agents for reads
Slug is generated from the name and is unique; name is required and unique
Colour is validated as a hex value and used consistently by the UI badges
Categories screen supports inline activate and deactivate plus drag-free sort_order editing
Deactivated categories disappear from the new-ticket dropdown but remain on existing tickets

stories.summary: Protect referential integrity on category delete
stories.want: deleting a category that still has tickets to be blocked or to require reassignment
stories.soThat: no ticket is ever orphaned and history stays readable
acceptanceCriteria: Deleting a category with tickets returns 422 explaining how many tickets block it
The response offers reassignment to another category, which moves the tickets and then deletes
Reassignment is wrapped in a transaction and logs an activity row on every affected ticket
A category with no tickets deletes cleanly as a soft delete

stories.summary: Cache master data in a Pinia store
stories.want: categories, priorities and statuses fetched once and shared across the app
stories.soThat: dropdowns and badges render instantly without repeated requests
acceptanceCriteria: A masterData Pinia store loads all three lists on first authenticated page load
Every dropdown and badge in the app reads from this store, never from its own request
The store exposes lookup helpers so a component can resolve an id to a name and colour
Mutating master data in the admin screens refreshes the store without a page reload

epics.goal: The core of the product: create tickets against a requester contact, then find, filter, search and read them efficiently.

stories.summary: Tickets and requesters schema with a readable reference
stories.want: the tickets and requesters migrations with proper indexes and a unique human-readable reference
stories.soThat: tickets can be cited by number in email and conversation, and queries stay fast
acceptanceCriteria: requesters table stores name, email (unique), phone and company as contact records with no login capability
tickets table carries reference, subject, description, requester_id, category_id, priority_id, status_id, assigned_to (nullable), created_by, the escalation columns and the resolved/closed timestamps
reference is unique and formatted TKT-YYYY-NNNNNN, generated inside a transaction so concurrent creates cannot collide
Indexes exist on status_id, category_id, priority_id, created_at and the composite (assigned_to, status_id)
A MySQL 8 FULLTEXT index covers subject and description
All foreign keys are constrained and tickets use soft deletes

stories.want: to create a ticket capturing the requester, subject, description, category and priority
stories.soThat: an incoming request is recorded and can be worked
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/tickets validates every field through a FormRequest and returns the created ticket resource
An existing requester is matched by email, otherwise a new requester contact is created in the same transaction
Status defaults to the is_default status and priority to the is_default priority when not supplied
created_by is taken from the authenticated user and can never be set from the request body
A created activity row is written for every new ticket
The create form validates client side, disables submit while in flight and cannot double-submit

stories.want: a paginated list of tickets showing the fields I triage on
stories.soThat: I can see the whole queue without scrolling forever
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/tickets returns a paginated resource collection with reference, subject, requester, category, priority, status, assignee and age
Related models are eager loaded so the endpoint issues a constant number of queries regardless of page size
Page size is configurable via a query parameter with a sane maximum
The table shows coloured status and priority badges and a relative age such as 3 days ago
Loading, empty and error states are all handled with distinct UI

stories.summary: Filter and sort the ticket queue
stories.want: to filter by status, priority, category, assignee and escalation state and to sort the results
stories.soThat: I can narrow thousands of tickets down to the ones I must act on
acceptanceCriteria: All filters compose on a single request and can be combined freely
Sorting is supported on created_at, updated_at and priority level, ascending and descending
Only whitelisted sort columns are accepted, so the parameter cannot be used for injection
Active filters are reflected in the URL query string so a filtered view can be bookmarked and shared
A visible clear-all control resets every filter at once

stories.want: to search by reference, subject, description or requester
stories.soThat: I can jump straight to a ticket a requester is asking about on the phone
acceptanceCriteria: A single q parameter searches the reference, subject, description and requester name and email
Subject and description use the FULLTEXT index rather than a leading-wildcard LIKE
Searching an exact reference returns that ticket first
Search composes with the existing filters instead of replacing them
The input is debounced so typing does not fire a request per keystroke

stories.want: a detail page showing everything about a ticket alongside the actions I can take
stories.soThat: I can understand and progress a ticket from one screen
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/tickets/{ticket} returns the full ticket with requester, category, priority, status, assignee and creator
The page shows all ticket fields, the escalation state and the resolved and closed timestamps when set
An action toolbar exposes assign, change status, escalate and edit, each hidden or disabled according to policy
Requesting a non-existent or soft-deleted ticket returns 404 and the SPA shows a not-found state
The page is reachable directly by URL and deep-links correctly after a reload

stories.want: to correct a ticket's subject, description, category or priority
stories.soThat: mistakes at intake can be fixed without losing the record
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{ticket} accepts partial updates and validates only what is sent
Every changed field writes its own activity row capturing the old and new values
Status and assignee cannot be changed through this endpoint; they have dedicated actions
reference, created_by and all timestamps are immutable through the API
The edit form pre-populates and warns before discarding unsaved changes

stories.want: to remove a ticket from the queue while keeping it recoverable
stories.soThat: spam and duplicates can be cleared without destroying data
acceptanceCriteria: DELETE /api/v1/tickets/{ticket} is admin-only and performs a soft delete
Soft-deleted tickets are excluded from all lists, filters, searches and statistics
An activity row records who deleted the ticket and when
The UI asks for confirmation naming the ticket reference before deleting

stories.want: a dashboard summarising the queue and my own workload
stories.soThat: I know where to start the moment I log in
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/tickets/stats returns counts grouped by status and by priority plus unassigned and escalated totals
Statistics are produced by aggregate queries, not by loading tickets into PHP
The dashboard shows my open tickets, the unassigned count and the escalated count as cards
Each card links through to the ticket list with the matching filter already applied
An agent sees their own workload while an admin sees the whole queue

epics.goal: Make ticket ownership explicit and visible: assign, claim, reassign, and see how work is distributed across agents.

stories.summary: Assign a ticket to an agent
stories.want: to assign a ticket to a specific agent
stories.soThat: every ticket has one accountable owner
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket}/assign sets assigned_to after validating the target is an active agent
Assigning to an inactive or non-existent user returns 422
An assigned activity row records the previous and new assignee
The assign modal lists only active agents, searchable by name
Assigning a ticket that is already assigned is treated as a reassignment, not an error

stories.want: to see unassigned tickets and claim one for myself
stories.soThat: new work is picked up without waiting for an admin
acceptanceCriteria: The ticket list offers an unassigned filter reachable in one click from the dashboard
An agent can claim an unassigned ticket, which assigns it to them
Claiming a ticket another agent already claimed returns a clear conflict message rather than silently overwriting
The claim action writes an activity row attributed to the claiming agent

stories.want: a view scoped to the tickets assigned to me
stories.soThat: I can focus on my own work without filtering every time
acceptanceCriteria: A My Tickets route pre-applies the assigned-to-me filter and excludes terminal statuses by default
The view reuses the same table and filter components as the main list rather than duplicating them
A toggle reveals my resolved and closed tickets
The sidebar shows a live count of my open tickets

stories.summary: Reassign or unassign with a reason
stories.want: to move a ticket to another agent or return it to the queue, recording why
stories.soThat: handovers are traceable rather than mysterious
acceptanceCriteria: The assign endpoint accepts a null user to unassign and return the ticket to the queue
An optional reason is stored on the activity row and shown in the timeline
Reassignment notifies the new assignee and does not notify the previous one twice
Both reassign and unassign are covered by feature tests

stories.want: to see how many open tickets each agent is carrying, broken down by priority
stories.soThat: I can rebalance before someone is overwhelmed
acceptanceCriteria: An endpoint returns open ticket counts per agent split by priority, using a grouped aggregate query
The screen highlights agents well above and well below the team average
Each agent row links to the ticket list filtered to that assignee
Inactive agents holding open tickets are surfaced so their work can be reassigned

epics.goal: A guarded status workflow that refuses illegal transitions, plus manual escalation that raises visibility and routes a ticket to an admin.

stories.want: a status_transitions table and a TicketWorkflow service that validates every status change against it
stories.soThat: the lifecycle is enforced by the server and stays configurable without code changes
acceptanceCriteria: status_transitions stores from_status_id, to_status_id and an optional required_role
Seeded edges implement New to Open to In Progress to Resolved to Closed, with Pending reachable from the active states and Reopened reachable from the terminal ones
TicketWorkflow exposes allowedTransitions(ticket, user) and assertCanTransition(...)
Any status change not present in the table is rejected with 422 and a message naming the attempted move
A transition whose required_role is admin is refused for agents
Unit tests cover both a legal and an illegal move for every seeded status

stories.want: to move a ticket to its next status, seeing only the moves that are legal from here
stories.soThat: I cannot put a ticket into an invalid state by accident
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket}/status transitions the ticket through TicketWorkflow
The ticket detail page offers only the transitions returned by allowedTransitions for the current user
Each change writes a status_changed activity row with the old and new status names
The UI reflects the new status immediately without a full page reload
A rejected transition surfaces the server message rather than a generic error

stories.want: to be required to explain the resolution when I resolve a ticket
stories.soThat: the record says how the problem was actually solved
acceptanceCriteria: Transitioning into Resolved requires a non-empty resolution note of a minimum length
resolved_at is stamped on the ticket and cleared if the ticket is later reopened
The resolution note is stored on the activity row and rendered prominently in the timeline
Transitioning into Closed stamps closed_at
first_responded_at is stamped the first time a ticket leaves the New status

stories.want: to reopen a resolved or closed ticket when the problem comes back
stories.soThat: a recurrence stays attached to its original history instead of starting a new ticket
acceptanceCriteria: A reopen transition is available from Resolved and Closed and requires a reason
Reopening clears resolved_at and closed_at and moves the ticket to Reopened
A reopened activity row is written with the reason
The detail page badges the ticket as reopened and shows how many times it has been reopened

stories.want: to escalate a ticket with a reason when I cannot resolve it at my level
stories.soThat: it reaches someone who can act instead of stalling silently
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket}/escalate increments escalation_level and stores escalated_at, escalated_by and escalation_reason
Escalation raises the priority by one level, stopping at the highest priority rather than overflowing
The ticket is routed to an admin, and the previous assignee is preserved in the activity trail
An escalated activity row captures the reason and the resulting escalation level
A terminal ticket cannot be escalated and returns 422
The reason is required with a minimum length

stories.summary: Escalated tickets are visible at a glance
stories.want: escalated tickets clearly marked and filterable
stories.soThat: the tickets that need me are never buried in the queue
acceptanceCriteria: The ticket list supports an escalated filter and shows an escalation badge with its level
The dashboard shows an escalated count that links to the filtered list
Escalated tickets can be sorted so the most recently escalated appear first
The badge visually distinguishes escalation level one from higher levels

stories.summary: Flag stale tickets on a schedule
stories.want: a scheduled command that flags tickets with no activity for N days
stories.soThat: nothing is quietly forgotten in the queue
acceptanceCriteria: An artisan command finds non-terminal tickets whose last activity is older than a configurable threshold
Each stale ticket receives a system activity row attributed to no user
The threshold and whether the command notifies are both configuration driven
The command is registered in the scheduler, is idempotent, and will not re-flag a ticket already flagged
Running the command with --dry-run reports what it would flag and changes nothing

epics.goal: An append-only record of every change to every ticket, surfaced as a readable timeline. This is the epic that makes the system auditable.

stories.summary: Activity table and a single recorder
stories.want: the ticket_activities table plus an ActivityRecorder that is the only code path writing to it
stories.soThat: the audit trail is complete by construction rather than by good intentions
acceptanceCriteria: ticket_activities stores ticket_id, nullable user_id, event, field, old_value, new_value, a JSON meta column and created_at
A backed enum defines every event type, so no raw event strings appear in the codebase
ActivityRecorder is the only class that inserts into ticket_activities, and TicketService is its only caller
A composite index on (ticket_id, created_at) keeps timeline reads fast
A null user_id means the actor was the system, and the UI renders it as such
Recording an activity happens in the same transaction as the change it describes, so the two can never disagree

stories.want: a chronological timeline on the ticket page showing who changed what and when
stories.soThat: I can understand a ticket's whole story before I act on it
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/tickets/{ticket}/activities returns activities newest first, paginated
Each entry renders as readable prose such as Ahmed changed status from Open to In Progress
Old and new values are shown for field changes, and the actor and relative time appear on every entry
Each event type has its own icon and colour so the timeline can be scanned quickly
System entries are visually distinct from user entries

stories.want: to add an internal note that appears in the timeline
stories.soThat: investigation and context are captured where the next agent will find them
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/tickets/{ticket}/notes stores the note body as a note_added activity
Note body is required, length validated, and escaped so no HTML or script can be injected
Notes are internal only and are never included in any email to a requester
Adding a note does not change the ticket status or its updated_at semantics for staleness
Notes appear inline in the timeline in correct chronological position

stories.want: activity records to be impossible to edit or delete
stories.soThat: the history can be trusted as evidence
acceptanceCriteria: No update or delete endpoint exists for ticket_activities anywhere in the routes file
The model blocks updates and deletes at the application level as a second line of defence
Soft-deleting a ticket preserves all of its activity rows
A feature test asserts that no route can mutate or remove an existing activity

stories.summary: Timeline stays usable on long-running tickets
stories.want: the timeline paginated and filterable when a ticket has hundreds of entries
stories.soThat: a long history does not make the page unusable
acceptanceCriteria: The timeline loads a first page and appends more on demand rather than loading everything
Entries can be filtered by event type, for example notes only or status changes only
A ticket with several hundred activities renders without a noticeable delay
The most recent entries are always visible first without extra interaction

epics.goal: Queued, retryable email on the events people care about, so a mail outage can never break a request or lose a notification.

stories.want: the database queue driver configured and Mailpit wired up in development
stories.soThat: mail is asynchronous and inspectable without sending anything real
acceptanceCriteria: Queue uses the database driver with the jobs and failed_jobs tables migrated
Development mail goes to Mailpit and no email can reach a real address from a dev environment
README documents running the queue worker and where to view captured mail
Failed jobs land in failed_jobs with their exception and can be retried by command

stories.summary: Notify an agent when a ticket is assigned
stories.want: an email when a ticket is assigned to me
stories.soThat: I learn about new work without watching the queue
acceptanceCriteria: Assignment dispatches a queued notification to the new assignee only
The email contains the reference, subject, priority, category, requester and a deep link to the ticket
No email is sent when a user assigns a ticket to themselves
Unassigning sends no email to anyone
A feature test asserts the notification is queued rather than sent synchronously

stories.summary: Confirm ticket creation to the requester
stories.want: a confirmation email carrying my ticket reference
stories.soThat: I have proof my request was logged and something to quote later
acceptanceCriteria: Creating a ticket queues a confirmation email to the requester's address
The email leads with the reference and echoes the subject and description as submitted
The email states expectations plainly and makes no promise about response time, since no SLA engine exists
A ticket created without a requester email queues nothing and logs the skip
No internal notes or agent-only information appear in the email

stories.summary: Notify the requester on status change and resolution
stories.want: an email when my ticket progresses or is resolved
stories.soThat: I do not have to chase anyone for an update
acceptanceCriteria: A status change to a requester-visible status queues an email naming the old and new status
Resolution email includes the resolution note
Which statuses are requester-visible is configuration driven, not hardcoded at the call site
Internal-only transitions send nothing
Rapid consecutive changes do not produce a burst of near-identical emails

stories.want: an email whenever a ticket is escalated
stories.soThat: escalations reach me even when I am not looking at the board
acceptanceCriteria: Escalation queues an email to all active admins
The email carries the reason, the escalation level, the requester and who escalated it
The subject line marks it as escalated so it can be filtered in a mail client
Escalating to level two or higher is visibly distinguished from a first escalation

stories.want: one Blade mail layout that every notification extends
stories.soThat: emails look consistent and render correctly across mail clients
acceptanceCriteria: A single layout provides the header, footer and ticket-summary block reused by all mailables
Emails render correctly on desktop and mobile widths and degrade gracefully without CSS
Every email has a plain-text alternative part
The from address, product name and base URL all come from configuration
No email leaks internal notes, agent email addresses or stack traces

stories.summary: Notifications are queued, retried and never break a request
stories.want: every notification dispatched from a queued job with retries and backoff
stories.soThat: a mail failure degrades quietly instead of failing the user's action
acceptanceCriteria: Every mailable is queued; no notification is sent inline during a request
Jobs declare tries and backoff, and exhausted jobs land in failed_jobs with context
A mail transport outage does not roll back or fail the ticket action that triggered it
Notifications dispatch after the database transaction commits, so no email references uncommitted data
Feature tests assert both the queued notification and its recipients for each event

epics.goal: Make the system demonstrable, tested, documented and safely deployable.

stories.want: model factories and a demo seeder producing a realistic dataset
stories.soThat: the app can be demonstrated and tested against believable data immediately
acceptanceCriteria: Factories exist for users, requesters, categories, tickets and activities
A demo seeder creates admins, several agents, a spread of categories and roughly fifty tickets across every status and priority
Seeded tickets have plausible activity histories, including some assigned, some escalated and some resolved
Created dates are spread over recent months so date filters and age columns are meaningful
The demo seeder is separate from the production seeder and never runs in production

stories.want: feature tests covering authentication, ticket CRUD, assignment, the workflow guard, escalation and activity logging
stories.soThat: the business rules stay true as the codebase grows
acceptanceCriteria: Authentication tests cover login, logout, rate limiting and the inactive-user case
Authorization tests assert an agent receives 403 on every admin-only endpoint
Workflow tests assert both a legal and an illegal transition for each seeded status
Escalation tests assert the level increment, the priority bump and its ceiling, and the activity row
Activity tests assert that every mutation path writes exactly the expected rows
The suite runs against MySQL in CI and passes from a clean database

stories.want: Vitest tests for the ticket table, the filters and the ticket form
stories.soThat: the components users touch most do not regress silently
acceptanceCriteria: TicketTable tests cover rendering, the empty state and the loading state
TicketFilters tests assert that changing a filter emits the expected query and that clear-all resets everything
TicketForm tests cover validation errors, a successful submit and the double-submit guard
The auth store is tested for login, logout and rehydration
npm run test:unit passes in CI

stories.want: generated API documentation covering every endpoint
stories.soThat: the frontend contract is explicit and does not have to be reverse-engineered
acceptanceCriteria: Every endpoint is documented with its method, path, parameters, request body and response shape
Authentication and the role requirement per endpoint are stated
Error responses, including validation 422 and authorization 403, are documented
docs/ contains the ERD and an overview of the ticket lifecycle
The documentation is generated or verified in CI so it cannot silently drift

stories.want: a documented, repeatable deployment path
stories.soThat: releasing is routine rather than an adventure
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend production build is verified and its output path documented
Runbook covers migrations, config and route caching, the queue worker and the scheduler as long-running processes
Every required production environment variable is listed with guidance, and debug mode is off
Rollback steps are documented, including how to reverse a migration
A first-deploy checklist covers creating the initial admin account safely

stories.want: a deliberate security review of the finished system
stories.soThat: obvious vulnerabilities are closed before anyone relies on this
acceptanceCriteria: Login and all write endpoints are rate limited
CORS is restricted to an explicit origin allowlist, never a wildcard in production
Every model defines fillable fields, so no mass-assignment hole exists on any request
All output is escaped and every user-supplied string in the timeline and ticket views is checked against XSS
No query concatenates user input; all filters and sorts use bindings or a whitelist
No secret, token or credential is present anywhere in the repository history
